ELE.scope_of_work: The electrical scope includes tower analysis and design modifications to accommodate increased ice and unbalanced ice loads. It also involves reviewing and proposing modifications to electrode suspension assemblies and designing fixes for the connection between tower top plates and double angles for specific tower types.
ELE.required_activities: Activities include analyzing and designing modifications for existing towers to handle increased and unbalanced ice loads, reviewing electrode suspension assemblies for stress reduction, and proposing and documenting design fixes for tower top plate connections. Deliverables include production drawings, installation procedures, and technical memos.

FND.scope_of_work: The foundation scope involves ensuring structural integrity for tower reinforcements and modifications to accommodate increased ice and unbalanced ice loads. This includes designing and analyzing foundations for tower modifications and ensuring compliance with design criteria.
FND.required_activities: Activities include designing and analyzing tower foundations to support reinforcements, preparing production drawings for foundation modifications, and ensuring compliance with technical specifications and design criteria. Deliverables include detailed drawings and installation procedures.

STR.scope_of_work: The structural scope includes designing reinforcements for existing towers to handle increased ice and unbalanced ice loads. It also involves addressing failures in tower components such as the OPGW tower peak and electrode crossarms.
STR.required_activities: Activities include analyzing and designing structural reinforcements for towers, addressing failures in tower components, and preparing production drawings and installation procedures for modifications. Deliverables include detailed structural designs and compliance with design criteria.

LN.scope_of_work: The line scope involves analyzing the feasibility of adding mid-span structures to reduce loads on towers and addressing issues related to unbalanced ice loads and ice shedding.
LN.required_activities: Activities include conducting feasibility studies for mid-span structures, analyzing line and tower requirements, and preparing technical memos with recommendations. Deliverables include analysis reports and recommendations for line modifications.

[None] SCOPE OF WORK

[None] Scope to include:

[None] Tower analysis and design modification of existing towers to accommodate increased ice and unbalanced ice loads. New design loads will be provided in table by vertical, transverse, and longitudinal at attachment points.

[None] Electrode suspension assembly design to be reviewed for length and articulation. There are concerns that the short length of suspension assembly is increasing stress and leading to failures on the conductor and crossarms. There is evidence that the conductor will come in contact with the insulator glass during unbalanced loading, and there are indications there is strain on the conductor at the clamp.

[None] Design fix for the connection between the towers top plate and the double angle that connects to the OPGW suspension assembly (see drawings below) for the remaining 4 tower types (the A2, A4, B1, and B2 towers). Through a failure investigation and FEM analysis it was determined the design of the connection details of the top plate and double angle, and the top plate itself of the several tower types are not adequate for the design load

[None] This design will have to be implemented on existing in-service structure. Hence The scope will include:

[None] Proposal of concept that will be adequate for the design loads and can be implemented on an existing in-service tower

[None] Analysis of concept

[None] Work procedure for installation

[ParagraphRole.SECTION_HEADING] BACKGROUND INFORMATION

[None] The Labrador-Island Transmission Link (LITL) is an important transmission line for the provincial energy grid due to its power carrying capacity that will be used to deliver a large portion of the winter peak energy and demand to the Island Interconnected System. Line L3501/2 is an overland transmission line that is a specific component of the LITL. It is an HVdc line between Muskrat Falls and Soldiers Pond that is to be operated at +/- 350 kV DC bi- pole, capable of transferring 900 MW. Traversing a distance of approximately 1,100 km through three major meteorological loading zones: average, alpine and eastern, The HVdc line has two pole conductors, one OPGW, and two electrode conductors for a portion of line on galvanized lattice steel towers. This line is constructed in harsh terrain subjected to heavy wind and ice loads, has been built since 2017, and has experienced multiple winter seasons and weather events.

[None] There were two failures on December 20th 2023 were the double angle that connects the OPGW assembly to the tower detached from the tower top plate. The failure investigation determined the root cause of the failure was an error in the design of the top plate connection. As part of the failure investigation a fix was design for the tower type that failed, Type A3, and an analysis of all other tower types was completed (A1, A2, A4, B1, B2). This analysis determined, there is a possibility of overload of the connection for the A2, A4, B1, and B2 tower. In order to address the findings from the failure investigation, an engineering design and repair procedure is required for fix of the top plate connection on the A2, A4, B1, and B2 towers.

[None] There have also been failures of tower components including the OPGW tower peak, and the electrode cross arm due to heavy ice loading, and unbalanced ice loads from ice shedding.

[None] Tower Reinforcement

[None] Tower reinforcement design shall include three separate designs as listed below, in addition to the original design load cases as per attached “350 kV HVdc Line Tower Type A1 Design Loading” drawings.

[None] Zone 1 reinforcements with two additional load cases

[None] Increased ice load on all wires of 63 mm of radial glaze ice.

[None] Unbalanced ice load with 63 mm of radial glaze ice and an unbalanced load of 70/100% on one electrode conductor

[None] Zone 10 reinforcement with two additional load cases:

[None] Unbalanced ice load with 50 mm of radial glaze ice and an unbalanced load of 50/100% on OPGW wire

[None] Unbalanced ice load with 55 mm of radial glaze ice and an unbalanced load of 70/100% on OPGW wire

[None] Zone 3a reinforcement with two additional load cases:

[None] Increased ice load on all wires of 70 mm of radial glaze ice, except a reduced ice load of 50 mm of radial glaze ice on the pole conductors

[None] Unbalanced ice load with 70 mm of radial glaze ice and an unbalanced load of 80/100% on OPGW wire, and a reduced ice load of 50 mm of radial glaze ice on the pole conductors
